data.screenshotMethod: Electron BrowserWindow.capturePage with exact content-size assertions for all zoom and project-command captures
data.scope: Real project-directory IPC, revision-bound pagination, scoped Unicode directories/junction exclusion, pointer and native ARIA tree keyboard input, selected-folder file creation/save, persisted editor drafts, keyboard file-tree visibility/cache/focus retention, actual application close/restart and dark minimum-window code/PTY input at 100/125/150 percent zoom. The sidebar stays visible; the file tree is manually hidden at 125/150 percent. Short-height layouts retain the add-project action. The populated long-name/path project dialog at 150 percent preserves complete field values and restores focus after Escape. PTY output is inspected while an actual Read-Host command awaits Enter, then returned to the project PowerShell prompt. Command-palette actions preserve the same live PTY and dirty editor contents, synchronize toolbar labels, retain choices across page navigation and disable unavailable contexts. An isolated held main-process IPC load proves that actual project removal invalidates an in-flight command. Owned read failures and a delayed directory response use isolated main-process fixtures. Physical folder picker, populated maximum-scale performance, full accessibility, full backup restore and other platforms remain separate checks.

scope: The actual newly built unpacked executable uses an owned empty standard-installation environment to exercise real legacy Windows PowerShell fallback. Seven focused project checks verify actual major-version output, scoped PTY commands, original prompt deadline, zoom/keyboard, restart and normal close with zero model requests. Original environment values are restored after the isolated test; this is a separate focused variant, not the complete 215-check distribution proof.
